Mtskheta-Mtianeti

The ancient capital Mtskheta and the Georgian Military Highway to Kazbegi — history and high mountains on one axis.

Click a marker for details. Coloured lines are ready-made road trips.

Mtskheta-Mtianeti starts immediately north of Tbilisi and runs up to the main ridge of the Caucasus. Its southern end is low and historic: Mtskheta, Georgia's first capital, with Svetitskhoveli Cathedral in the middle of town, and above it on a rock spur the Jvari Monastery, looking down on the confluence of the Aragvi and the Mtkvari. Both are UNESCO-listed and both are half an hour from the capital.

North of that begins the Georgian Military Highway, the country's most famous drive. The green water of the Zhinvali Reservoir, the fortified complex of Ananuri on its shore, then a long climb to Gudauri — a ski resort in winter, and in summer the way to the Russia-Georgia Friendship Monument and the Jvari Pass at 2,379 metres. Beyond the watershed lies Kazbegi: the town of Stepantsminda, Gergeti Trinity Church at 2,170 metres against the cone of Mount Kazbek, the Dariali Gorge and the Gveleti waterfalls.

The side valleys are a different world again. Truso opens west of the highway with mineral springs and rust-coloured travertine terraces. In Khevsureti, Shatili is a village built as a single mass of stone towers near the northern border, reached over a high unpaved pass.

Seasonality is sharp. Mtskheta, Ananuri and Zhinvali are open all year; Gudauri runs from December to March for skiing; Truso and Shatili are realistically June to September. Half a day covers Mtskheta, a full day gets you to Kazbegi, and a night in Stepantsminda makes it far better.

Best for

  • Half a day in Mtskheta for Svetitskhoveli and Jvari
  • A two-day run to Kazbegi with an overnight stop
  • Skiing at Gudauri between December and March
  • Summer 4x4 trips into Truso and Khevsureti

Driving conditions

The Military Highway (S3) is paved for its whole length, but it is a mountain road and behaves like one. The stretch between Gudauri and Kobi is avalanche-prone, and in heavy snow the police close it for hours or days at a time; winter tyres are required from November to March and chains are worth carrying. Queues of freight lorries heading for the Dariali border crossing are common and make overtaking awkward on the narrow sections.

The last six kilometres up to Gergeti Trinity are steep and badly broken — you need real ground clearance or one of the local jeeps. Truso and Shatili are unpaved and 4x4 only; the Datvisjvari Pass towards Shatili is usually open from June to October. Fill up in Pasanauri or Gudauri. The classic mistake is attempting Kazbegi as a winter day return and crossing the pass in the dark.
